verdict: 2026-08-03 06:37:28 PDT — The per-(AC, surface) model is proportionate for this instruction-driven repository, and no dependency manifest or existing library supplies the missing denominator. However, I would tighten the shape before adopting it globally: preserve the approved plan through one explicit amendment log, keep surfaces distinct from verification mechanisms and policy limits, and remove a self-referential reviewer oracle.

findings.title: Append-only tables lack an explicit amendment model
findings.locus: In scope 3; AC3; Design sketch — Steps 8–9
findings.claim: The sketch makes arbitrary Markdown rows append-only and permits retractions to be appended, but it does not define where amendments live, how a retraction identifies its target, or how a reader derives the active plan when free-text surface names repeat or change. Git already preserves the approved `spec:` version, while this repository conventionally records later decisions in dedicated appended sections. Making future authors encode state transitions inside each AC table creates an ambiguous cross-cutting protocol.
findings.alternative: Freeze the approved per-AC tables and add one declarative `Falsification-plan amendments` log. Each entry should state action (`add` or `retract`), AC, exact surface/target, reason, and `added at: implement`; demonstrate-red records then reference active additions. Use the `spec:` commit as the immutable baseline.
findings.win: Centralizes all post-approval changes in one section, gives every retraction an unambiguous target, removes mixed active/retracted state from arbitrary tables, and reuses the repository's existing immutable git baseline.

findings.title: The example collapses surfaces, oracles, and known limits
findings.locus: Test notes introduction; AC2–AC4 `surfaces excluded` entries
findings.claim: The contract defines a surface as where the criterion is observable, but its canonical example calls the gate a recurring surface and lists reviewer judgment quality and the volume of implementation-added rows as excluded surfaces. Those are respectively an oracle/mechanism quality and a policy limit, not criterion-derived product observables. Because future stories will copy this example, the model invites authors to enumerate tests and reviewers instead of the criterion's extent—the implementation anchoring this story is intended to prevent.
findings.alternative: Reserve surface rows and `surfaces excluded` exclusively for criterion-derived observables. Put unverifiable oracle quality, amendment-volume concerns, and similar assurance limits in the existing Honest limit or Non-goals text, with reasons, rather than representing them as excluded surfaces.
findings.win: Restores one invariant for every row, removes three category exceptions from the example, and prevents future plans from appearing complete by listing verification machinery instead of omitted product surfaces.

findings.title: AC4 assigns the reviewer as oracle for its own omission
findings.locus: Test notes — AC4, `reviewer output on a future story` row
findings.claim: The planned regression is that the reviewer never flags an under-enumerated plan, while the named oracle is that same reviewer. An oracle that fails in the regression cannot detect the regression; the note that no repository oracle proves reviewer behavior accurately admits that this row has no oracle. This conflicts with the inherited requirement that every planned regression name the mechanism that catches it.
findings.alternative: Keep AC4's gate row for prompt removal or weakening. Either remove the future-behavior row because AC4 only requires the prompt, or classify an independent human/second-reviewer inspection of produced review output as `manual`; do not label the failing reviewer itself as the oracle.
findings.win: Eliminates one impossible detection path and ensures every retained falsification row names an independent mechanism capable of observing its regression.
